newsitem.title: USA: Catastrophe Exchange completes first transaction.
newsitem.headline: Catastrophe Exchange completes first transaction.

text.p: The Catastrophe Risk Exchange Inc (Catex) said $4 million of reinsurance coverage was provided to a primary insurer in the electronic risk trading system's first transaction.
A total of $4 million in coverage was provided in a deal in which Transatlantic Holdings Inc's Transatlantic Reinsurance Co sold an Industry Loss Warranty policy to a client of Aon Corp's Aon Re.
The policy sold was to provide payment to the primary insurer, an Aon Re client, in the event of an insured market loss in the United States and the Caribbean of $20 billion or more, Catex said.
Catex, which was approved by New York insurance regulators in 1995 and launched operations last year, allows subscribers to swap or sell catastrophic risk exposures over a nationwide computer system.

Although other deals have been made, in part, by using information provided by Catex, "this is the first transaction to be carried all the way through the system from beginning to end," said Catex president Samuel Fortunato.
"It is the first of many, many many more to come," Fortunato said.
The first transaction was signaled by a response originating in the Londom market to a posting of an anonymous offer to assume coverage, Catex said.
Catex offers subscribers the capability of anonymously posting offers to assume or cede coverage or exchange risks.
A dialogue followed and eventually parties came to an agreement about the scope of the coverage and the price involved.
Although the parties involved in the transaction are Catex subscribers, the deal was done on behalf of an insurer that does not subscribe to Catex.
"We are particularly pleased with the emergence of market loss warranties as an early trading opportunity on Catex," said Catex chief executive Frank Fortunato.

Using the Catex facility, insurers can quickly obtain covers to supplement their annual catastrophe reinsurance programs or respond to strong hurricanes forming in the Atlantic or Gulf of Mexico, he said.
Market loss warranties are reinsurance contracts where loss payments are triggered in part by an index measuring aggregate industry claims for a particular event.
Catex said it has over 30 subscribers and said it has begun to see postings of offers to provide reinsurance to cover hurricane loss for periods as short as the duration of specifically named events.

Meanwhile, Catex Bermuda, a joint venture between Catex and the Bermuda stock exchange, has moved closer to meeting its September opening date after the Bermuda parliament approved a bill allowing the creation of the offshore electronic risk exchange, Catex said.

Also, Catex said it completed a two week demonstration of its system at Lloyd's of London on July 25. Catex said it has been discussing options which would provide system access to the 120 Lloyd's syndicates, 60 managing general agents and 120 Lloyd's brokers.
